To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the five career patterns are associated with different leisure lives; and (b) leisure activities and attitudes are associated with self-concept and career patterns.

the five post-16 careers are distinguished by their different leisure patterns and attitudes; the five post- 16 careers are distinguished in terms of the leisure patterns and attitudes they engender; the five post–16 careers are distinguished from one another in terms of the different leisure patterns they engender; and the five post-19 careers are distinguished from each other in terms of the attitudes and self-concept they engender.

the career pattern of a person in the 16–19 age range is closely related to the type of leisure activity he or she engages in, and the type of leisure activities a person in the age range engages in is closely related to that person's career pattern.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the leisure behaviour of young men and women aged 16 to 18 years varies according to the different career paths that they follow.
the interrelationship between work and leisure and the way in which these are experienced in the context of the life course.
the interrelationship between career and leisure and with the ways in which leisure contributes to the formation of a lifestyle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leisure behaviour of young men and women in the different career patterns is not only different but is also a function of their attitudes and self-concept, and vice versa.

the career patterns are not simply reflections of different levels of educational and vocational attainment, but are also associated with different lifestyles, different leisure patterns and different orientations to the future.
young people's leisure activities, attitudes and self-concept are strongly influenced by their career plans and experiences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the young people's leisure behaviour is a function of their career pattern and the attitudes and self-concept they develop are related to the leisure activities in which they engage.

the career patterns are associated with different types and amounts of leisure, different types of friends and leisure companions, different attitudes towards leisure and work and different types of self-concept.
the leisure lives of the different career patterns are very different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the young people's career patterns and leisure lifestyles are closely interwoven and mutually reinforcing.
the leisure activities young people engage in, and the attitudes and values they hold, are strongly associated with their post-16 career choices.
the career patterns are not just different in the labour market but also in the way young people live their lives.
